lines: +This GitHub composite action starts a standalone Nacos server for the config e2e suites. Run it after the KinD cluster exists.
+- Runs `nacos/nacos-server` on the `kind` Docker network, publishing ports 8848 and 9848 on the runner
+- Waits until the server is ready, printing its log if it never is
+- Exports `NACOS_ADDR` (how the suite on the runner reaches it) and `NACOS_POD_HOST` (how the controller's pods reach it)
+The specs of `test/e2e-config-test` that need Nacos skip when these are not set; the config upgrade job requires them, and sets `NACOS_CLI_HOST` itself for the old CLI.
+description: 'Starts a standalone Nacos server on the kind network and tells the e2e suites where it is'
+    # Pods reach the container by name: kind's CoreDNS forwards to the node's resolver, which is
+    # Docker's DNS on the kind network. The suite itself reads Nacos from the runner.
+  # Weekly, for the config upgrade job: changes outside its paths can break that path too
\ No newline at end of file
+  # Config upgrade from 1.11 and rollback (#7410's verification plan). A paths
+  # filter here rather than on the trigger, which would also gate the job above.
+      # The 1.11 CLI publishes to Nacos from the runner and the controller from a pod: the
+      # container's address on the kind network serves both.
+      - name: Build the branch CLI, fetch the ${{ env.OLD_VERSION }} CLI
+          # as deploy-latest-release: the released chart can't finish a fresh install on
+          # Kubernetes 1.36+ with secure TLS for cluster-gateway (#7452)
+      - name: Upgrade to the current branch
+      - name: Checks after the upgrade, migration, the gate, Nacos
+          for phase in after-upgrade migrate gate nacos; do
+      # The chart no longer ships definitions as Helm objects, so the first rollback fails on
+      # them ("no ComponentDefinition with the name ...") and records the old manifest. Helm's
+      # diff then no longer sees the webhook entries the branch added: deleting the configuration
+      # lets the second rollback recreate it as 1.11.0 has it.
+          if ! out=$(helm rollback kubevela 1 -n vela-system --wait --timeout 6m 2>&1); then
+            echo "$out" | grep -q "no ComponentDefinition with the name"

+// The markers GitOps and release tools leave on what they apply.
+// EventMigratedGitOpsManaged is recorded on the CR that adopted a legacy object a GitOps or
+// GitOpsManager names the tool whose marker obj carries and the marker itself, or two empty
+// strings. The vela CLI never sets these markers on a legacy config object, so a match means a
+// person or a tool put it there, and a tool that applies an object applies it again: the owner
+// should keep the new CR where the legacy object is kept. Helm itself stamps managed-by=Helm on
+// what it installs; the instance label comes from a chart's templates. app.kubernetes.io/instance
+// without it is what Argo CD's label tracking sets, and also what many charts and hand-written manifests
+// set, so it is reported as possible, not as Argo CD.
+		return "Argo CD (label tracking) or another tool", "label " + instanceLabel
+// gitOpsNote is the line a migration adds, to its report row and to a MigratedGitOpsManaged
+// Event on the new CR, when the legacy object it adopted carries a tool's marker; "" when it
+// carries none. kind is the legacy object's kind, crKind the CR's.
+func gitOpsNote(legacy metav1.Object, kind, crKind string) string {
+	case "Argo CD (label tracking) or another tool":
+		return fmt.Sprintf("the legacy %s may be managed by %s (%s): if so, keep this %s where it is kept instead, so the next sync does not reapply the legacy object", kind, tool, marker, crKind)
+	return fmt.Sprintf("the legacy %s is managed by %s (%s): keep this %s where it is kept instead, so the next sync does not reapply the legacy object", kind, tool, marker, crKind)
